questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial clause.

Which option demonstrates correct inversion for emphasis of the time clause?

A. Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
B. So fast did the car go that it almost crashed.
C. Hardly had I arrived when the meeting started.
D. Only after checking the documents did I realize the mistake.
options: Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
So fast did the car go that it almost crashed.
Hardly had I arrived when the meeting started.
Only after checking the documents did I realize the mistake.
questions.answer: Only after checking the documents did I realize the mistake.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight specific information?

Select the option that uses a cleft sentence structure to emphasize the location of the event.

A. It was in London that the conference took place.
B. The conference took place in London, but we don't know where.
C. London was the venue for the conference.
D. The conference was in London, that is certain.
options: It was in London that the conference took place.
The conference took place in London, but we don't know where.
London was the venue for the conference.
The conference was in London, that is certain.
questions.answer: It was in London that the conference took place.

questions.question:
Choose the option that correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical or non-factual condition.

Which sentence uses the subjunctive correctly to express a contrary-to-fact scenario?

A. If I were you, I would accept the job offer.
B. If I was you, I would accept the job offer.
C. If I had been you, I would have accepted the job offer.
D. If I am you, I will accept the job offer.
options: If I were you, I would accept the job offer.
If I was you, I would accept the job offer.
If I had been you, I would have accepted the job offer.
If I am you, I will accept the job offer.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would accept the job offer.

questions.question:
Select the sentence that correctly demonstrates ellipsis, where a word is omitted but understood from context.

Which option correctly uses ellipsis to maintain grammatical coherence?

A. She finished her homework, and so did her brother.
B. She finished her homework, and her brother did too.
C. She finished her homework, and her brother finished too.
D. She finished her homework, and her brother also did.
options: She finished her homework, and so did her brother.
She finished her homework, and her brother did too.
She finished her homework, and her brother finished too.
She finished her homework, and her brother also did.
questions.answer: She finished her homework, and so did her brother.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses a complex sentence structure with multiple clauses to convey a nuanced meaning?

Select the option that appropriately combines two ideas using a subordinating conjunction to express a cause-effect relationship.

A. Because of the rain, the match was postponed.
B. The match was postponed because the rain.
C. The match was postponed because of the rain.
D. Because rain, the match was postponed.
options: Because of the rain, the match was postponed.
The match was postponed because the rain.
The match was postponed because of the rain.
Because rain, the match was postponed.
questions.answer: The match was postponed because of the rain.
